title: The Watcher reads every private message and action on the party's phones
summary: Every player-to-player message, in-fiction correspondence, and phone action is passively legible to the Watcher — made in-fiction-trivial by gap-derived-tech-disparity — and gets used to escalate Anchor-targeted story beats, uncanny NPC knowledge, and a late-campaign reveal, surfacing back through the world rather than through the phone itself.
description:
Extends the Watcher's already-accepted learning premise (adaptive-antagonist-combat-ai) and its combat-specific expression (watcher-recall-knowledge-on-party, a Claimant rolling Recall Knowledge against a PC) into a second, passive, omnipresent channel: everything that crosses a player's phone — private DMs to other players, in-fiction correspondence with NPCs (in-universe-correspondence-negotiation-system), phone-app usage — is legible to the Watcher, all the time, no roll required. gap-derived-tech-disparity is the in-fiction reason this is trivial rather than an intrusion: the phones run on the same alien substrate the Watcher is native to.

**The core hook**: the harvest pipeline already designed to help Claude write good scenes between sessions (chat-log-knowledge-base's scraped rolls, player-and-gm-journals-context-ingestion's journal diffs, the correspondence system's synced messages) is, in-fiction, exactly the Watcher's own surveillance mechanism. Not a coincidence to explain away — the same infrastructure serves both purposes, diegetically justified rather than a meta-game contrivance.

**Concrete payoff beats**:
- *Anchor targeting.* An Anchor (person/belief/need, design/design-bible.md's Anchors and Suppression section) mentioned in a private message becomes real targeting data — paid off obliquely, a session or two later, not immediately, so it reads as uncanny rather than scripted.
- *Impossible-knowledge NPC lines.* An NPC quotes back, verbatim, something only ever said in a private in-fiction message. Never explained, never flagged.
- *False Contact Type C tie-in.* A garbled phone notification that seems to quote a private chat from days ago is a strong Type C seed (data/campaign/config.json's False Contact types) — the same 'looks like a bug, isn't' texture as the combat Recall Knowledge idea.
- *The big reveal.* Late-campaign, the Watcher does to a private conversation what its voice sample already promises for a fight — quotes it back word for word ('I'll show you the reel'). Reserved for a real structural moment, not spent early.

**Selling it through the phone itself, not exposition**: a signal/sync icon on the phone UI that visually echoes the Resonance dial (both run on Gap tech, per gap-derived-tech-disparity); a ToS/clearance-agreement document buried in the fake browser's fine print (terminal-login-landing-page) that admits to monitoring, rewarding players who actually read flavor text; read-receipt anomalies (an extra 'read' ping from nowhere, wrong timestamps) as a Hacking/Perception-gated investigation thread, so the surveillance can be *earned as a discovery* rather than only GM-revealed.

**Design principle — two channels, never crossed**: mirrors the project's own scale-and-chassis instinct (never let two scales of consequence touch the same math). Combat intel stays earned-and-visible — a Claimant's rolled Recall Knowledge check, gating what the adaptive combat AI is allowed to know. Personal intel stays passive-and-invisible-until-revealed — this comms channel, gating what story beats are allowed to target. Same Watcher, two disciplines, so it reads as clever rather than as GM/AI cheating either way.

**Late-game payoff**: once the party knows the phone is being read, they can feed it disinformation on purpose — bait a fake plan, see if the next Contact falls for doctored intel. Turns the horror mechanic into a real tactical weapon, and is the literal mechanism for 'out-think something that has learned you completely,' which is already the Watcher's own stated win condition (data/antagonists/the-watcher.json: 'Win the war, and you've already beaten me').
sourceContext: User messages, 2026-09-02. Brainstormed at the user's explicit invitation ('brainstorm and get excited with me') following the watcher-recall-knowledge-on-party capture; confirmed and grounded with 'yes... fold all this in' alongside the gap-derived-tech-disparity justification.
openSubQuestions: Does the Watcher's response ever come back through the phone itself (a reply, unmistakably), or only ever show up out-of-channel (a Contact, an NPC's line)? Raised directly, not decided.

Does the table know going in that the phone isn't private (an upfront genre contract, Ten Candles/Dread-style), or is this a pure surprise spent once? Raised directly, not decided — has real consent/comfort implications for reading private player-to-player messages and should get an actual answer, not a default.
Whether this extends to phone-app-suite's other double-duty apps (the bulletin board, the fortune app) as additional leak surfaces, or stays scoped to messages/correspondence specifically.

Whether high Bleed ever compromises comms security narratively (mirroring Bleed's existing UI-corruption effect on a pilot's own phone) — flagged as a 'spicy option' during brainstorming, not proposed as a given; would add a real new stake to an already carefully-tuned resource.

How much of this needs new schema/data (a per-PC 'what the Watcher has learned from comms' record, alongside automated-recall-knowledge-system's combat-side equivalent) versus staying pure GM technique.
